_readme.purpose: RadiusOS clinical insight rules. Dictation stream -> trigger -> measurement + context -> recommendation text.
how_it_works: 1. If any trigger phrase is heard, the rule activates.
2. Extract the size nearest the trigger and convert to mm (cm x 10). If several lesions are dictated, use the 'measure.use' value (largest or most_suspicious).
3. Read context words (from dictation, clinical history, or order indication) to fill each context key.
4. Walk 'recommendations' top to bottom; the first one whose 'when' conditions all match is output.
5. If a key listed in 'ask_if_missing' is not found, show that prompt instead of guessing.
6. Match the longest phrase first (e.g. 'bosniak 2f' before 'bosniak 2').
7. An empty 'when': {} is the default and always matches; keep it last.
8. 'defaults' fills a context key when nothing is dictated.
9. A rule with 'derive' computes a context key (e.g. TI-RADS level, Bosniak class) from dictated features when the key itself was not dictated.

condition_keys.solid_gt / solid_gte / solid_lt / solid_: solid component size in mm (part-solid nodules)
condition_keys.any other key: must equal the context value, e.g. "menopause": "post"

Category 3 or 4 nodule stable at 3 or more months is downgraded (stepped management).
4X = category 3 or 4 nodule with additional suspicious features (spiculation, lymphadenopathy) - radiologist assigned.
S modifier for clinically significant non-lung-cancer findings.

Juxtapleural (including perifissural) nodule: category 2 only when solid, smooth, oval/lentiform/triangular and smaller than 10 mm. At 10 mm or larger no row fires; describe and score it as a solid nodule.

rules.finding: Lung-RADS category stated by the radiologist (0, 4X, S)
rules.applies_to: Categories the radiologist assigns that size cannot compute: 0 (incomplete), 4X (additional suspicious features), S (other significant findings).

recommendations.output: Lung-RADS 0, incomplete: part or all of the lungs cannot be evaluated, or prior chest CT examinations are being located for comparison. Recommend additional lung cancer screening CT images and/or comparison with prior chest CT examinations.

Lung-RADS 4X, very suspicious: category 3 or 4 nodule with additional features or imaging findings that increase the suspicion of malignancy. Recommend diagnostic chest CT with or without contrast, PET/CT and/or tissue sampling, depending on the probability of malignancy and comorbidities; PET/CT may be used when there is a solid component of 8 mm or larger.
Lung-RADS S modifier: potentially clinically significant findings unrelated to lung cancer are present and are addressed separately in this report. Manage as appropriate to the specific finding.

notes: A 4XS dictation reads as 4X, the more suspicious statement; dictate the S finding's own recommendation separately.

recommendations.output: Solid nodule smaller than 6 mm: no routine follow-up for a low-risk patient; optional non-contrast chest CT at 12 months for a high-risk patient (Fleischner 2017).
Solid nodule 6-8 mm: non-contrast chest CT at 6-12 months. If stable, a further CT at 18-24 months is optional for a low-risk patient and recommended for a high-risk patient (Fleischner 2017).
Solid nodule larger than 8 mm: for low-risk and high-risk patients alike, consider chest CT at 3 months, PET/CT, or tissue sampling (Fleischner 2017).

Multiple solid nodules smaller than 6 mm: no routine follow-up for a low-risk patient without a known or suspected primary cancer; optional non-contrast chest CT at 12 months for a high-risk patient (Fleischner 2017).

Multiple solid nodules 6-8 mm: non-contrast chest CT at 3-6 months. If stable, a further CT at 18-24 months is optional for a low-risk patient and recommended for a high-risk patient (Fleischner 2017).

Multiple solid nodules, largest more than 8 mm: non-contrast chest CT at 3-6 months. If stable, a further CT at 18-24 months is optional for a low-risk patient and recommended for a high-risk patient (Fleischner 2017).
Ground glass nodule smaller than 6 mm: no routine follow-up (Fleischner 2017).
Ground glass nodule 6 mm or larger: CT at 6-12 months to confirm persistence, then CT every 2 years until 5 years of stability (Fleischner 2017).
Part-solid nodule smaller than 6 mm: no routine follow-up (Fleischner 2017).

Part-solid nodule 6 mm or larger: non-contrast CT at 3-6 months to confirm persistence. If unchanged and the solid component stays below 6 mm, annual CT for 5 years. A persistent nodule with a solid component of 6 mm or larger is highly suspicious (Fleischner 2017).
Multiple subsolid nodules less than 6 mm: CT at 3-6 months; if stable, consider CT at 2 and 4 years (Fleischner 2017).
Multiple subsolid nodules: CT at 3-6 months; subsequent management based on the most suspicious nodule (Fleischner 2017).

notes: Persistent part-solid nodules with solid component 6 mm or larger are highly suspicious.

rules.guideline: ACR Incidental Findings Committee white paper 2017 (Megibow et al., JACR 2017;14:911-923)

recommendations.output: Thoracic aortic aneurysm 4.0 cm or larger with acute symptoms or findings: recommend urgent cardiothoracic or vascular surgery consultation, if not already performed.
Aortic root, ascending or arch aneurysm 4.5 cm or larger with chronic risk factors: recommend cardiothoracic or vascular surgery consultation, if not already performed.

Aortic root, ascending or arch aneurysm 4.5 cm or larger without risk factors: recommend cardiothoracic or vascular surgery consultation and CT or MRI if not already performed, with imaging surveillance by CT or MRI starting at 6-12 months.
Aortic root, ascending or arch dilatation 4.0-4.4 cm: consider cardiothoracic or vascular surgery consultation. Recommend imaging surveillance by CT or MRI starting at 6-12 months.

Descending thoracic aortic aneurysm 4.0 cm or larger with chronic risk factors: consider vascular surgery consultation, if not already performed. Recommend imaging surveillance by CT or MRI starting at 6-12 months.

Descending thoracic aortic aneurysm 4.5 cm or larger without risk factors: recommend vascular surgery consultation, if not already performed, and imaging surveillance by CT or MRI starting at 6-12 months.

Descending thoracic aortic dilatation 4.0-4.4 cm without risk factors: consider vascular surgery consultation, if not already performed. Recommend lifelong imaging surveillance by CT or MRI starting at 6-12 months to evaluate for growth or new wall abnormalities.
Thoracic aortic aneurysm 5.0 cm or larger: recommend vascular surgery consultation, if not already performed.
Thoracic aortic aneurysm 4.0-4.9 cm: recommend vascular surgery consultation and CT or MRI if not already performed, with imaging surveillance by CT or MRI starting at 6-12 months.

notes: Below 4.0 cm no row fires. Unspecified-location rows have a 4.0 cm floor so a normal aorta is never referred.
